title: Panchavati
hook: on the road to a new home, a giant bird lands in front of them and says he knew their father
carry: a brother builds a house with his hands

segments.voice: Yesterday: Agastya's weapons. The sage who digested a demon gave Rama Vishnu's bow and sent him on to Panchavati: they come with a blessing, not a grudge.

Halfway there, a huge bird settles on a tree in front of them. A vulture, enormous and old. After Viradha, Rama's first thought is a rakshasa in disguise, and he asks who it is. The bird answers gently. I was a friend of your father, he says. My name is Jatayu. And he offers what no one else has: when you two brothers go out into the forest, I'll stay and watch over Sita.
screen: `A GIANT BIRD ON A TREE.` → `I WAS YOUR FATHER'S FRIEND.` → `I'LL WATCH OVER SITA.`

segments.voice: Jatayu, the vulture king, gives his lineage, a long one reaching back to the beginning of creatures. Hearing that he was Dasharatha's friend, Rama embraces him. It's a brief meeting, but hold on to it: of everyone in the forest book, this old bird's promise to guard Sita will cost the most. Then they reach Panchavati, usually explained as the place of five banyan trees. It sits on the Godavari, with flowering trees, deer, peacocks, and mountains in the distance. Rama turns to Lakshmana: you choose the spot. Lakshmana would rather be told. As long as you live, he says, I'm here to do what you ask. So Rama picks a level place near the water, and Lakshmana builds the hut. Valmiki describes it with pleasure: walls of packed earth, posts of bamboo, a roof of leaves and long grass, a floor made smooth. Then Lakshmana bathes in the river, gathers flowers and fruit, and makes an offering for the new home. Rama is moved. He holds his brother and says something close to this: with you here, it's as if our father is not gone. That's the heart of Panchavati. Not the scenery, lovely as it is, but a brother building a house with his own hands so the family has a place to live again.
screen: `JATAYU, THE VULTURE KING.` · `PANCHAVATI: FIVE BANYANS.` · `YOU CHOOSE. NO, YOU TELL ME.` · `LAKSHMANA BUILDS THE HUT.` · then, large: `WITH YOU, OUR FATHER IS NOT GONE.`

segments.voice: Feel the room around you and find one thing someone made or fixed with their hands: a chair, a shelf, a meal on the stove. Then bring to mind someone who built you a place to land, literally or not, and let their face come. Breathe in thanks, and breathe out ease.
Panchavati. Five banyans by the Godavari, where Lakshmana builds a hut and Rama says: with you here, our father is not gone.
Your line: a brother builds a house with his hands. And an old bird has promised to keep watch. I'm glad you came.

howItsDone: Panchavati is identified by many pilgrims with a site at Nashik on the Godavari, and the hut Lakshmana builds is a favorite scene in Ramayana art and performance.

chat.says: Why does Rama get so emotional over a little hut in the forest?
options: Lakshmana built it with his own hands, and with him there, Rama says, their father feels near.
The hut was a gift from Agastya, the first home anyone had given them in exile.
Sita chose the spot herself, and it reminded Rama of the palace back in Ayodhya.
chat.meaning: Lakshmana asked Rama to choose, then built the hut himself. Rama held him: with you here, it's as if our father is not gone.

Viradha.meaning: the forest giant who seized Sita days before

rakshasa.meaning: a demon-like being of the forest and of Lanka
